'''James L. Gould''' (born July 31, 1945) is an American [[Ethology|ethologist]], [[Evolutionary biology|evolutionary biologist]], and popular science writer. He has served as a professor of [[ecology]] and evolutionary biology at [[Princeton University]] since receiving his [[PhD]] in 1975.<ref name="vita">{{cite web |url=https://eeb.princeton.edu/sites/eeb/files/people-cv/CV_2.pdf |title=''Curriculum Vitae''|website=Princeton University}}</ref> However, he is primarily known for the experiment he designed while an undergraduate at [[Caltech]] which proved that bees use [[Waggle dance|complex dances]] to [[Bee learning and communication|communicate the location of food]].<ref>{{cite journal |author=Gould JL |year= 1975 |title=Honey bee recruitment: the dance-language controversy |journal=[[Science (journal)|Science]] |volume=189 |pages=685–693| doi = 10.1126/science.1154023 |url=http://isites.harvard.edu/fs/docs/icb.topic46718.files/gould-controversy.pdf|issue=4204|pmid= 1154023 |bibcode= 1975Sci...189..685G }}</ref> In addition to several technical works and textbooks, he co-wrote with his wife the popular science book ''The Honey Bee''.<ref name="The Buzz on James Gould">{{cite web|url=https://www.princeton.edu/~stcweb/html/pope04essay.html |title=''The Buzz on James Gould'' |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120107053947/http://www.princeton.edu/~stcweb/html/pope04essay.html |archivedate=2012-01-07 }}</ref>

Gould went on to do work that further specialized in communication in [[southern right whales]]. He also published studies that made serious contributions to the ethological understanding of [[animal navigation]] and [[sexual selection]].

During his long career at Princeton, Gould has been dedicated to teaching as well as research. Notably, he taught introductory biology and animal behavior courses, as well as field courses in [[marine biology]].

==Selected publications==

*''The Honey Bee'' (1988)
*''Animal Architects: Building and the Evolution of Intelligence'' (2007)
